evals.prompt: I want to show real-time progress of a long-running Trigger.dev task in my Next.js React app. The task processes a batch of items and I want a progress bar. How do I set this up?
evals.expected_output: Should cover: auth.createPublicToken, useRealtimeRun or useRealtimeTaskTrigger hook, metadata for progress, @trigger.dev/react-hooks
expectations: Includes auth token creation (createPublicToken or createTriggerPublicToken)

evals.prompt: My Next.js app triggers a Trigger.dev task from a Server Action and shows the run with useRealtimeRun. It works against Trigger.dev Cloud but against our self-hosted server the hook never gets any data, and long runs stop updating after a few minutes. What is wrong?
evals.expected_output: baseURL on the hook (or TriggerAuthContext) for self-hosted, NEXT_PUBLIC address, publicAccessToken lifetime and refreshAccessToken, no TriggerProvider
expectations: Says the hook needs baseURL pointing at the self-hosted server because the browser has no TRIGGER_API_URL and the default is Trigger.dev Cloud
Puts the address in a NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable and keeps TRIGGER_SECRET_KEY on the server

Explains that the publicAccessToken from the trigger() handle is short-lived: the docs say 15 minutes, and the SDK signs a 1 hour token itself when the server sends no x-trigger-jwt, so the publicAccessToken request option applies only in that case

Adds a refreshAccessToken callback that calls a server function which authorizes the caller (a run tag set at trigger time and checked with runs.retrieve, or a token scoped to the user's tag) before minting a token with auth.createPublicToken
Uses TriggerAuthContext.Provider or per-hook options and does not use a TriggerProvider component
